summary_en: Osaka Steel will acquire up to 8 billion yen worth of shares from parent Nippon Steel at a discount to market price via public offer, representing approximately 26.8% of shares outstanding (excluding treasury stock), as part of a capital return program capped at 8 billion yen for fiscal 2026-2027.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Treasury Stock and Public Offer for Purchase of Treasury Stock
translation_en_brief:
On November 4, 2026, Osaka Steel's board of directors resolved to acquire treasury stock from its parent company Nippon Steel via public offer. This acquisition is part of the company's capital return program capped at 8 billion yen for fiscal years 2026-2027, following an earlier acquisition of 9 million shares (22.05 billion yen) completed in April 2025.

The company determined that acquiring shares from Nippon Steel, which owns 16,629,030 shares (55.58% ownership), is appropriate because it protects the company's free-float ratio. Osaka Steel's free-float ratio stood at 28.54% as of March 31, 2026. Acquiring shares from minority shareholders would reduce this ratio below the 25% minimum required by Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market listing rules, potentially jeopardizing the company's listing. By acquiring from Nippon Steel, which already holds shares not counted in the free-float calculation, the listing status is preserved.

The company will use public offer methodology to ensure transaction transparency and fair pricing. The acquisition price will be set at approximately 10% discount to market price, determined by analyzing 122 comparable cases of treasury stock public offers resolved after January 1, 2022. This discount level was most commonly used, appearing in 88 of the 122 precedent cases studied. The specific share quantity and acquisition price will be determined based on market conditions at the time of execution.
